title: SSE chunk resequencer and atomic tool-call coordinator for OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Background: Customers using our OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility layer are observing two classes of failures when proxying streaming responses from Redwood models back to legacy clients: 1) SSE chunk reordering and split boundaries that cause malformed JSON tokens or truncated function call payloads on client side; 2) function/tool-calls emitted across multiple non-atomic chunks that result in duplicated tool invocations or partially applied arguments. Goal: Implement a lightweight resequencer + coalescer in the compatibility gateway that (a) reorders and reassembles out-of-order SSE chunks deterministically, (b) stitches split JSON tokens without buffering entire responses, and (c) provides an atomic tool-call coordinator that folds multi-chunk function call emissions into a single canonical tool invocation with idempotency keys and token-level provenance. Non-goals: Full protocol redesign of client SDKs, rewriting client-side parsers. This is an interstitial compatibility shim limited to the gateway layer.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy clients relying on OpenAI Chat Completions SSE must successfully parse streamed responses that previously failed due to split JSON tokens (no parse error in sampled regression tests)
Tool/function-call sequences that were previously split across multiple SSE events are coalesced into a single logical invocation with an idempotency key, preventing duplicate downstream tool runs
Latency inflation introduced by the resequencer must be <= 15ms p95 for median sized responses (<= 256 tokens) under normal load
End-to-end E2E tests that simulate 3 concurrent perturbed chunk orders pass consistently in CI
implementation_notes: Add a deterministic sequence buffer keyed by stream_id + chunk_seq_hint. The buffer will accept out-of-order chunks and emit in-order frames when contiguous windows are available.
Use a small sliding window (default 4 frames) with a fast-path for in-order append to avoid allocations for common case; window size configurable by feature flag.

Detect split JSON tokens by scanning chunk boundaries for open/close braces and quotation states; attempt local token reassembly up to a 2KB threshold, then fall back to 'chunk-boundary marker' wrapper if exceeded.

Function-call folding: when an incoming chunk contains a partial function call object (tool name + partial args), hold until the object closes or threshold reached; then synthesize a single 'tool_call' envelope with idempotency key derived from conversation_id + sequential_counter.
Emit instrumentation: counters for resequenced_frames, coalesced_tool_calls, dropped_frames, and increases in p95 latency. Expose metrics in /metrics and Console dashboard.

Backward-compatibility: maintain original SSE event names and order semantics for clients that rely on strict event ordering—feature gate via header x-rw-compat-mode=resequencer to opt-in per-customer until rollout.

Failure modes: on window timeout (no contiguous next chunk) emit best-effort partial frame with a debug header and log for post-mortem; provide a customer-visible flag for strict vs best-effort behavior.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-scan boundary algorithm covering nested JSON, escaped quotes, unicode boundaries
Property-based tests that generate random chunk splits and reorderings to assert deterministic reassembly
Integration tests using a fake model backend that intentionally emits out-of-order SSE frames and split function calls
Load test scenario in staging simulating 500 concurrent streams with 20% perturbed chunk reordering to validate latency and memory behavior
Regression suite against existing legacy clients (internal harness) to confirm no behavioral regressions
rollout_plan: Feature-flag deploy to gateway canary hosts (10% traffic) for 48 hours with enhanced logging
If metrics show <0.5% error delta and latency within budget, increase to 50% for 24 hours
Follow with account-level opt-in for customers with known compatibility incidents before global enablement
Post-rollout: remove debug headers after two weeks and monitor for 30 days for any customer-reported parsing anomalies
comments: 2025-02-13 Owen Patel: Spike complete. Prototype resequencer using ring buffer behaves well for in-order common case. Observed memory spike with 16KB window on synthetic stream — will cap to 4KB by default.

2025-02-18 Marisol Vega (PM): Confirmed two enterprise customers reported duplicate tool invocations — the folding approach with idempotency key should address this. Please add an audit event when a folded tool-call is emitted.

2025-02-21 Design review (Anika Shah): UX note — Console should surface a per-stream 'compat shim applied' flag and a breadcrumb to the original SSE chunks for debugging. Adding as follow-up (ENG-524683).

2025-02-24 Security (Jamal Reed): Reviewed approach for idempotency keys; ensure we use non-sensitive deterministic hashing (sha256(conversation_id + nonce)) and avoid embedding user prompt content in the key. OK to proceed with privacy guardrails.
2025-02-27 Infra (Liu Chen): Gateway CPU p95 increased by 6% in canary due to extra parsing—plan to offload heavy scanning to a native extension if p95 > 10% at scale. Track as dependency ENG-524684.
2025-03-01 Owen Patel: Working on PR. Added initial metrics and unit tests. Need review on token boundary scanner implementation details. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2786
